title: 2014 AMC8 21
statement: The \(7\)-digit numbers \(\underline{74A52B1}\) and \(\underline{326AB4C}\) are each multiples of \(3\). Which of the following could be the value of \(C\)?

solutions.text:
For \(\underline{74A52B1}\) to be divisible by \(3\), the digit sum \(19+A+B\) must be a multiple of \(3\). Hence \(A+B\) is \(1\) less than a multiple of \(3\).

For \(\underline{326AB4C}\) to be divisible by \(3\), the digit sum \(15+A+B+C\) must be a multiple of \(3\). Since \(15\) is already divisible by \(3\), \(A+B+C\) must be divisible by \(3\).

Therefore \(C\) must be \(1\) more than a multiple of \(3\). Among the answer choices, only \(1\) has that form.

Thus, A is the correct answer.
hints: Use the divisibility-by-\(3\) test on both numbers.
Compare what the first number says about \(A+B\) with what the second number needs.
